rules.title: Ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data to set rents
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use algorithmic devices that use nonpublic competitor information to advise on rent or occupancy. Tenants may sue for damages, an injunction, and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, with each unit and each month counted as a separate violation.
rules.key_value: Up to $1,000 per violation; each unit-month a separate violation
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords of residential dwelling units in San Francisco.
rules.quoted_span: The ordinance prohibits landlords from using qualifying algorithmic devices that calculate nonpublic competitor information to advise on rent or occupancy.
rules.penalty: Damages, injunctive relief, civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each month of use per affected unit may be a separate violation (S.F. Admin. Code § 37.10C(b), (d)).

rules.title: Ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices using nonpublic competitor data
rules.requirement: Landlords in San Diego may not use the restricted algorithmic rent-pricing devices. Tenants may sue for damages, an injunction, and penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, with each month and each affected property possibly counted as a separate violation.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords of residential rental properties in San Diego.
rules.quoted_span: San Diego similarly authorizes tenant suits for damages, injunctive relief and penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, with each month and affected rental property potentially constituting a separate violation.
rules.penalty: Damages, injunctive relief, penalties up to $1,000 per violation (San Diego Mun. Code §§ 98.1103(b), 98.1104(a)).

rules.title: Ban on coordinated pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: Landlords in Berkeley may not use coordinated rent-pricing algorithms. Tenants have private remedies, and each unit and month of use can be a separate violation.
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits coordinated pricing algorithms; recurring unit/month violations and private remedies, previously at issue in
rules.conflict_note: RealPage challenged the ordinance in RealPage, Inc. v. City of Berkeley (N.D. Cal.). Per this source, that case was voluntarily dismissed with prejudice on Jan. 14, 2026, so the ordinance appears to stand.

rules.title: Ban on automated rent price-fixing
rules.requirement: Landlords in Santa Ana may not use the specified anticompetitive automated rent price-fixing. Tenants may sue for up to $1,000 per violation for each month.
rules.key_value: Up to $1,000 per violation and per month
rules.quoted_span: Ordinance NS-3090 prohibits specified anticompetitive automated rent price-fixing; private tenant claims and up to $1,000 per violation and per month.
rules.penalty: Private tenant claims; up to $1,000 per violation and per month.

rules.title: Ban on algorithmic rent coordination services
rules.requirement: Landlords in Jersey City may not use algorithmic rent coordination services. Both the city and private parties can enforce the ban, with fines of up to $2,000 per day.
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits a landlord’s use of algorithmic rent coordination services; includes public and private enforcement; fines up to $2,000 per day.
rules.penalty: Fines up to $2,000 per day; public and private enforcement.

rules.title: Ban on software/algorithms coordinating rents
rules.requirement: Landlords in Hoboken may not use software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms to coordinate or recommend rents, lease terms, or occupancy.
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits landlords from using software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms to coordinate or recommend rents, lease terms, or occupancy.

notes: Secondary source (Morgan Lewis LawFlash, Aug. 21, 2026), so confidence is lowered for all records. Each in-scope ordinance appears only as a summary in a table row, and some appear in the case discussion too. Effective dates are often given only to the month. Exemptions and coverage thresholds are not described for any in-scope ordinance, so check them against the official text. Left out because they are outside our jurisdictions: Seattle, King County, Spokane, Philadelphia, Minneapolis, Providence, Portland, Rockville, and pending measures in Montgomery County MD, Evanston IL and Rhode Island. The article mentions that 'states' have enacted algorithmic pricing laws but names no CA, NJ or MA state statute, so no state records were made. The Jersey City listing was the document's reason for inclusion. Its citation (§ 218-12) and its fine ($2,000 per day) come only from this summary. The article also notes that these local ordinances may face challenges to municipal authority, but it identifies no specific preemption conflict for the in-scope cities.
